condition: Ruptured haemorrhagic corpus luteum cyst on a DOAC
permutationLabel: Haemoperitoneum from a corpus luteum cyst in a woman on apixaban
summary: 38-year-old woman on apixaban for DVT, sudden right pelvic pain on day 22 of her cycle, light-headed, HR 118, BP 96/60, Hb 9.4 (13.1 last month); urine hCG negative; US: haemorrhagic right ovarian cyst with free fluid in the pelvis and Morison's pouch.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Sudden right lower abdominal pain and feeling faint
inputs.hpi: Sudden right lower abdominal and pelvic pain 6 hours ago during intercourse, day 22 of a regular cycle. Now light-headed on standing and has right shoulder-tip pain. On apixaban 5 mg twice daily for a DVT 4 months ago (after a leg fracture); last dose 3 hours ago. Urine hCG negative.

exam.abdomen: Tender right iliac fossa and suprapubic region with guarding; mild distension.

imaging.name: USS pelvis (transvaginal)
imaging.result: 4 cm right ovarian cyst with reticular (lace-like) internal echoes consistent with a haemorrhagic corpus luteum; moderate echogenic free fluid in the pelvis extending to Morison's pouch (haemoperitoneum). Normal uterus, no intrauterine or adnexal pregnancy.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Ruptured haemorrhagic right corpus luteum cyst with haemoperitoneum — on apixaban
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Haemoperitoneum from a ruptured haemorrhagic corpus luteum cyst in a woman on apixaban, haemodynamically compromised. Resuscitate, crossmatch, withhold apixaban and consider reversal (andexanet / PCC) with haematology; gynaecology for laparoscopy if ongoing bleeding.

redFlags.note: Active bleeding on a factor Xa inhibitor must be flagged.

mustInclude.note: Major bleeding on apixaban: consider reversal (andexanet alfa or 4-factor PCC) with haematology.

guideline.name: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 174 — evaluation and management of adnexal masses
guideline.section: Pregnancy test in reproductive-age women with an adnexal mass and pain; transvaginal ultrasound; haemorrhagic corpus luteum cysts are usually managed conservatively unless haemodynamic compromise
guideline.citation: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. Evaluation and management of adnexal masses: Practice Bulletin No. 174. Obstet Gynecol. 2016;128:e210–e226.

guideline.name: 2020 ACC expert consensus decision pathway — management of bleeding in patients on oral anticoagulants
guideline.section: Major bleeding on a factor Xa inhibitor: stop the anticoagulant, supportive care and transfusion, consider reversal (andexanet alfa or 4-factor PCC); source control
guideline.citation: Tomaselli GF, Mahaffey KW, Cuker A, et al. 2020 ACC expert consensus decision pathway on management of bleeding in patients on oral anticoagulants. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2020;76:594–622.

guideline.name: NICE NG126 — ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage: diagnosis and initial management
guideline.section: Pregnancy test in every woman of reproductive age with abdominal/pelvic pain, even with contraception; transvaginal ultrasound; immediate referral to an early pregnancy assessment service / gynaecology when pregnancy test positive with pain; surgical management if ruptured
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage: diagnosis and initial management. NICE guideline NG126, 2019 (updated 2023).

rationale: A corpus luteum haemorrhage is usually self-limiting, but on a DOAC it can cause shock. The anticoagulant must be recognised, stopped and possibly reversed, with blood available and gynaecology involved.
